metadata.scope: e_goryeo (all 150 baronies across k_baekje, k_goguryeo, k_silla)

schema_notes.is_historical_867: true if the barony name is attested as a settlement/fortress/administrative unit by <= 867 CE; false if first attested post-867 CE or unattested.
schema_notes.older_name_by_867: Tracks attested pre-867 CE names for the same site or immediate predecessor when distinct from the barony name.
schema_notes.natural_proper_name: true only when the toponym directly adopts a specific proper hydronym, oronym, choronym, or named topographic feature (excluding directional/locator compounds).

b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Cheongju.first_mention_attestation: 940 CE (Goryeo Taejo 23), when Seowon-gyeong was renamed Cheongju (淸州), recorded in Goryeosa Geography.
b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Cheongju.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean administrative name 'Clear Prefecture' (淸州), bestowed by Goryeo Taejo in 940 CE. Prior to 940 CE, the site was Baekje Sangdang-hyeon (上黨縣), established by Unified Silla as Seowon-sogyeong (西原小京) in 685 CE and renamed Seowon-gyeong (西原京) in 757 CE.

older_name_by_867.notes: Renamed Seowon-gyeong in 757 CE before becoming Cheongju in 940 CE.

b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Yeonsan.first_mention_attestation: 940 CE (Goryeo Taejo 23), when Silla Hwangsan-gun was renamed Yeonsan-hyeon (連山縣), recorded in Goryeosa Geography.
b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Yeonsan.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean administrative name 'Connected Mountains' (連山), bestowed by Goryeo Taejo in 940 CE (note: the repo's b_hanzi '燕山' is a homophone substitution for historical 連山). Before 940 CE, it was Baekje Hwangdeungyasan-gun, renamed Hwangsan-gun (黃山郡) by Silla King Gyeongdeok in 757 CE.

older_name_by_867.notes: Renamed Yeonsan-hyeon in 940 CE.

b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Seorim.first_mention_attestation: 757 CE (Silla Gyeongdeok 16), when Baekje Seollim-gun was renamed Seorim-gun (西林郡), recorded in Samguk Sagi Geography.
b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Seorim.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean directional compound 'West Forest' (西林), coined in 757 CE as a Silla standardization of Baekje Seollim-gun (舌林郡), itself interpreted as a phonetic/semantic rendering of a native Baekje toponym meaning 'prosperous settlement'.

b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Chungju.first_mention_attestation: 940 CE (Goryeo Taejo 23), when Silla Jungwon-gyeong was renamed Chungju (忠州), recorded in Goryeosa Geography.
b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Chungju.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean administrative name 'Loyalty Prefecture' (忠州), granted by Goryeo Taejo in 940 CE. Earlier, the site was Goguryeo Gugwon-seong (國原城), made Silla Gugwon-sogyeong (國原小京) in 557 CE, and renamed Jungwon-gyeong (中原京) in 757 CE.

older_name_by_867.notes: Renamed Jungwon-gyeong in 757 CE and Chungju in 940 CE.

b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Goeju.first_mention_attestation: 940 CE (Goryeo Taejo 23), when Silla Goeyang-gun was renamed Goeju (槐州), recorded in Goryeosa Geography.
b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Goeju.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean administrative name 'Pagoda-Tree Prefecture' (槐州, modern Goesan), bestowed by Goryeo Taejo in 940 CE (note: the repo's b_hanzi '高州' confuses Chungcheong's 槐州 with Hamgyeong's Goju 高州). Earlier it was Goguryeo Inggeunnae-gun, renamed Goeyang-gun (槐壤郡) in 757 CE.

older_name_by_867.notes: Renamed Goeju in 940 CE.

b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Jangyeon.first_mention_attestation: 1018 CE (Goryeo Hyeonjong 9), when former Goguryeo Sangmo-hyeon was renamed Jangyeon-hyeon (長延縣) and attached to Chungju, recorded in Goryeosa Geography.
b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Jangyeon.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean auspicious administrative name 'Long Extension' (長延), created in 1018 CE under Goryeo Hyeonjong for the former Goguryeo county of Sangmo-hyeon (上芼縣) in modern Goesan-gun.

b_Goryeo_Gyeongsang_Boryeong.first_mention_attestation: 1018 CE (Goryeo Hyeonjong 9), when Silla Sin'eup-hyeon was renamed Boryeong-hyeon (保寧縣), recorded in Goryeosa Geography.
b_Goryeo_Gyeongsang_Boryeong.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean auspicious administrative name 'Preserve Peace' (保寧), established in 1018 CE under Goryeo Hyeonjong (note: the repo key's 'Gyeongsang' and b_hanzi '报令' are misplacements/homophone errors for Chungcheong's 保寧). Earlier it was Baekje Sinchon-hyeon, renamed Sin'eup-hyeon in 757 CE.

older_name_by_867.notes: Renamed Boryeong-hyeon in 1018 CE.

b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Gongju.first_mention_attestation: 940 CE (Goryeo Taejo 23), when Silla Ungju was renamed Gongju (公州), recorded in Goryeosa Geography.
b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Gongju.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean administrative name 'Duke Prefecture' (公州), bestowed by Goryeo Taejo in 940 CE. Earlier, the site was the Baekje capital Ungjin (熊津, 475 CE), Silla Ungcheon-ju (熊川州, 686 CE), and Ungju (熊州, 757 CE).

b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Nampo.first_mention_attestation: 757 CE (Silla Gyeongdeok 16), when Baekje Sapo-hyeon was renamed Nampo-hyeon (南浦縣), recorded in Samguk Sagi Geography.
b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Nampo.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean directional locator compound 'South Estuary' (南浦), coined in 757 CE under Silla King Gyeongdeok to replace the Baekje county name Sapo-hyeon (寺浦縣).

older_name_by_867.notes: Renamed Nampo-hyeon in 757 CE.

b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Cheonan.first_mention_attestation: 930 CE (Goryeo Taejo 13), when Goryeo Taejo established Cheonan-bu (天安府) in the Dosol region, recorded in Goryeosa.
b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Cheonan.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean auspicious administrative name 'Heavenly Peace' (天安), coined in 930 CE when Goryeo Taejo merged surrounding districts into Cheonan-bu. Prior to 930 CE, the area was known as Dosol (兜率) and flanked by Daemogak-gun (Silla Daerok-gun, 757 CE) and Sasan-hyeon (687 CE).

older_name_by_867.notes: Cheonan-bu was newly created in 930 CE from the Dosol area and neighboring Silla counties.

b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Yesan.first_mention_attestation: 919 CE (Goryeo Taejo 2), when Silla Gosan-hyeon was renamed Yesan-hyeon (禮山縣), recorded in Goryeosa Geography.
b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Yesan.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean auspicious administrative name 'Rites Mountain' (禮山), bestowed by Goryeo Taejo in 919 CE. Earlier, it was Baekje Osan-hyeon (烏山縣), renamed Gosan-hyeon (孤山縣) by Silla King Gyeongdeok in 757 CE.

b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Hongju.first_mention_attestation: 1012 CE or shortly thereafter (Goryeo Hyeonjong 3+), when Unju (運州) was reorganized and renamed Hongju (洪州), recorded in Goryeosa Geography.
b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Hongju.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean administrative name 'Vast Prefecture' (洪州), adopted under Goryeo Hyeonjong (1012 CE or shortly after) to replace Unju (運州). In 660 CE, the Hongju area hosted the Silla-Tang staging camp Sarajijeong (沙羅之停).

older_name_by_867.notes: Became Unju in the early 10th century and Hongju in/after 1012 CE.

b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Buseong.first_mention_attestation: 757 CE (Silla Gyeongdeok 16), when Baekje Gi-gun was renamed Buseong-gun (富城郡), recorded in Samguk Sagi Geography.
b_Goryeo_Yanggwan_Buseong.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean auspicious administrative name 'Wealthy Citadel' (富城), coined in 757 CE by Silla King Gyeongdeok to replace Baekje Gi-gun (基郡, modern Seosan).

older_name_by_867.notes: Renamed Buseong-gun in 757 CE.

b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Jeonju.first_mention_attestation: 757 CE (Silla Gyeongdeok 16), when Wansan-ju was renamed Jeonju (全州), recorded in Samguk Sagi Geography.
b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Jeonju.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean administrative name 'Complete Prefecture' (全州), adopted in 757 CE under Silla King Gyeongdeok's sinification of the Nine Provinces, replacing Wansan-ju (完山州, established 685 CE) via a semantic shift from 完 ('complete') to 全 ('whole').

older_name_by_867.notes: Renamed Jeonju in 757 CE, though Wansan remained in concurrent use.

b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Yeonggwang.first_mention_attestation: 940 CE (Goryeo Taejo 23), when Silla Muryeong-gun was renamed Yeonggwang-gun (靈光郡), recorded in Goryeosa Geography.
b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Yeonggwang.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean auspicious administrative name 'Numinous Radiance' (靈光), bestowed by Goryeo Taejo in 940 CE. Earlier it was Baekje Muho'i-gun (武戶伊郡), renamed Moji (牟支) in 660 CE and Muryeong-gun (武靈郡) in 757 CE.

b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Gangseong.first_mention_attestation: 757 CE (Silla Gyeongdeok 16), when Baekje Gosaburi-gun was renamed Gobu-gun (古阜郡), recorded in Samguk Sagi Geography.
b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Gangseong.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean administrative name 'Ancient Mound' (古阜, Gobu), created in 757 CE as an abbreviated sinification of Baekje Gosaburi-gun (古沙夫里郡, 'Old Sand Village'). Note: the repo's barony_key/modern_name uses 'Gangseong', which does not match b_hanzi '古阜' and appears to be a key mislabeling.

older_name_by_867.notes: Renamed Gobu-gun in 757 CE.

b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Jillye.first_mention_attestation: 757 CE (Silla Gyeongdeok 16), when Baekje Jinnae-gun (進乃郡) was formally renamed Jillye-gun (進禮郡), recorded in Samguk Sagi Geography.
b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Jillye.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean auspicious administrative name 'Advance Rites' (進禮), coined in 757 CE as a phonetic-semantic sinification of Baekje Jinnae-gun / Jiningeul-gun (進乃郡 / 進仍乙郡), which was captured by Kim Yu-sin in 648 CE.

b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Jindong.first_mention_attestation: 757 CE (Silla Gyeongdeok 16), when Baekje Jindong-hyeon (珍同縣) was retained under Hwangsan-gun in Ungju, recorded in Samguk Sagi Geography.
b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Jindong.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean transcription of a Baekje county name (珍同縣 / 珍洞縣), retained unchanged by Silla King Gyeongdeok in 757 CE.

b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Mupung.first_mention_attestation: 757 CE (Silla Gyeongdeok 16), when Silla Musan-hyeon was renamed Mupung-hyeon (茂豐縣), recorded in Samguk Sagi Geography.
b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Mupung.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean auspicious administrative name 'Luxuriant Abundance' (茂豐), coined in 757 CE under Silla King Gyeongdeok to replace Musan-hyeon (茂山縣).

older_name_by_867.notes: Renamed Mupung-hyeon in 757 CE.

b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Namwon.first_mention_attestation: 685 CE (Silla Sinmun 5), when Silla established Namwon-sogyeong (南原小京) on former Baekje Goryong-gun, recorded in Samguk Sagi.

older_name_by_867.notes: Became Namwon-sogyeong in 685 CE and Namwon-gyeong in 757 CE.

b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Imsil.first_mention_attestation: 757 CE (Silla Gyeongdeok 16), when Baekje Imsil-gun (任實郡) was retained under Wansan-ju, recorded in Samguk Sagi Geography.
b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Imsil.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean transcription of a Baekje commandery name (任實郡), retained unchanged by Silla King Gyeongdeok in 757 CE.

b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Jinan.first_mention_attestation: 757 CE (Silla Gyeongdeok 16), when Baekje Nanjina-hyeon was renamed Jinan-hyeon (鎭安縣), recorded in Samguk Sagi Geography.
b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Jinan.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean auspicious administrative name 'Garrison Peace' (鎭安), coined in 757 CE by Silla King Gyeongdeok to replace Baekje Nanjina-hyeon / Wollyang-hyeon (難珍阿縣 / 月良縣).

older_name_by_867.notes: Renamed Jinan-hyeon in 757 CE.

b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Boseong.first_mention_attestation: 757 CE (Silla Gyeongdeok 16), when Baekje Bokhol-gun was renamed Boseong-gun (寶城郡), recorded in Samguk Sagi Geography.
b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Boseong.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean auspicious administrative name 'Precious Citadel' (寶城), coined in 757 CE by Silla King Gyeongdeok to replace Baekje Bokhol-gun (伏忽郡).

b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Seungpyeong.first_mention_attestation: 757 CE (Silla Gyeongdeok 16), when Baekje Gampyeong-gun was renamed Seungpyeong-gun (昇平郡), recorded in Samguk Sagi Geography.
b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Seungpyeong.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean auspicious administrative name 'Ascending Peace' (昇平), coined in 757 CE by Silla King Gyeongdeok to replace Baekje Gampyeong-gun / Mupyeong-gun / Sapyeong-gun (欿平郡 / 武平郡 / 沙平郡).

b_Goryeo_Jeolla_Namyang.etymology_analysis: Sino-Korean directional compound 'South Sunny Slope' (南陽), bestowed by Goryeo Taejo in 940 CE. Earlier it was Baekje Jojorye-hyeon (助助禮縣), renamed Chungnyeol-hyeon (忠烈縣) by Silla King Gyeongdeok in 757 CE.
